chunks: And Zurārah narrated from one of them, peace be upon them:
Regarding four men who testified against a woman for zinā, and she said, "I am a virgin," so the women examined her and found her to be a virgin, he said: "The testimony of the women is accepted."

key_terms.الزِّنَا: illicit sexual intercourse, the accusation under consideration
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman, the person accused in the case
key_terms.بِكْرٌ: a virgin, the woman’s claim concerning her physical state
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurārah, the narrator transmitting from one of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.شَهِدُوا: they testified or bore witness in a legal case

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women accepted in an adultery accusation case in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling in a case where four witnesses accused a woman of zinā, but female examiners found her to be a virgin. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the testimony of the women is accepted in this matter, showing the evidentiary value of women’s testimony in issues specifically connected to female bodily examination.
